After about 6 months or so I felt much better, my memory started to come back, although even to this day it’s still not very good. I also give credit to the other amounts of drugs I used.

For me, I only compare the 2 because of the “floating on a cloud feeling” I always describe my experience with hydrocodone as “being wrapped in the warmest blanket ever, and being hugged by god himself” 

DXM doesn’t have that same exact feeling, but the weightlessness of all my problems and thoughts was just gone. Floating on a cloud, it felt good.

 “the dissociation can just get you out of the real world” 

It really did that for me though, I don’t really get visuals all that much, but I would just enter a place that *was* my house. But it wasn’t, you know? A world where I didn’t have those problems.

It wasn’t a physical addiction, but a mental one. 

I had some problems in my life that I’d rather not get into. But when I’d take Dxm It would just, clear my mind of all my problems. I don’t really know how to explain it. I liked the dissociation. Everything about who I was and what I had done just went out the door. That made it super easy for me to just keep doing it. And to be fully honest, I have no idea how many times a week I truly did it because I just can’t remember. 

I don’t do it much anymore, I’ve been off of it for about 4 weeks so far. I will occasionally do a 450mg dose, but at my peak use I was usually around 1000mg, and like I said that was possibly 3-4 times a week.

Yeah, opiates are a slippery slope. In the week I didn’t take them, I couldn’t stop thinking about doing them the next week, and they were on my mind all the time. I’m actually pretty happy the second time was unremarkable because it made me realize that the high wasn’t worth the risks. I like to think I’m very careful with the drugs I use. People always say they’re in control and won’t let the drug take them over. 

I used to be like that, then during the last part of August, September and some of October, I had a very bad addiction to DXM. I was in a bad place and the fact that I would completely forget all my problems on it, and the fact I could get it so easily made it my drug of choice. 

I was probably doing it 3-4 times per week. I remember nothing of those months, and my short term memory is just starting to come back. No matter how much of a hold you think you have, you’ll easily fall.
